note: Feel numbers that are not physical (physical ones live in reality.json). Camera rows sized against hero.height 1.89 m.

camera.note_pitch: pitch_max: degrees the follow view may look up; 35 showed little more than the horizon and the night sky could not be watched (Ravindu, 14 Nov). Looking up, the arm shortens against the ground and the hero fades (fade_near, fade_far)
camera.note_fade: fade_near and fade_far: m from the lens to the hero's drawn box, gone from fade_near in, solid from fade_far out, the whole body as one in between (it was a per-pixel dither by each fragment's distance, which showed as a dot pattern over the pack and helmet in a tight room). lift_full: m of free arm behind the pivot at which a wall behind lifts the view all the way to pitch_min
camera.note_follow: follow_rate: 1/s, the pivot's critically damped spring (it trails a steady walk by 2 v / rate); follow_limit: m it may trail; rise_rate: 1/s, the pivot's height toward the floor, slower than across; lead_time: s of velocity the aim looks ahead in a steady run; lead_rate: 1/s, how slowly that lead builds and goes; recentre_after: s of no look input before the yaw drifts behind the real travel; recentre_per_m: rad of drift per rad of error per metre travelled (a leash, so it never turns while the hero stands or pushes a wall)
camera.note_glance: the dusk hint (follow_cam.gd glance, the targets from audio/audio.gd: the habitat, and the dust devil when it is out, in the sunset sky only, the hero on foot outside), art direction after Nesky's 50 Camera Mistakes #30 to #36 (design/research/pages/alive/camera.md): far targets turn the view, never take control, never while the player looks. glance_after: s of no look input, standing, before it starts; glance_deg_s: how slowly it turns (the whole 6 degrees in 7.5 s, a drift, not a camera move); glance_max_deg: the most it turns until the player looks again; glance_front_deg: only toward a target within this many degrees either side of the view, so it never swings round to something behind
camera.note_rush: a vehicle's speed framing (follow_cam.gd), reached at its top speed and eased by lead_rate: rush_distance and rush_height are shares of the vehicle distance and pivot height (9 m and 2.4 m become 7.2 m and 1.9 m), rush_lead s of velocity the aim looks ahead (lead_time on foot). The field of view never changes (skills/third-person-camera rule 14). Our choice, 13 Nov playtest: "I felt the rover is slow"
camera.note_clear: the lens kept out of everything, with no pop (follow_cam.gd, tests/camera_test.gd; Ravindu, 14 Nov: 'whenever the camera hits an object behind it, the camera glitches ... we don't need to show the skeleton of the model'). clear: m, the radius of the sphere the arm and the feelers cast, so the lens rests that far from every solid: more than twice the near plane's half-diagonal (0.083 m at 16:9), so the near plane cannot cut into a wall or a prop and show its hollow inside (it was that half-diagonal plus 1 cm, and anything drawn a centimetre proud of its collider was cut open). A cut by the arm goes at once to where the near plane is clear and takes the rest of the sphere at feel_rate. skin: m the arm's root and the pivot stop short of a wall they are pushed toward (the shoulder offset, the pivot trailing the hero): left touching it, a turn of a few degrees took the arm from full length to nothing; in_shoulder_clear: the same for the shoulder offset, wider, so that in a 1.2 m doorway the arm's root stays within 0.1 m of the middle and the feelers have room either side (with the root hard by the frame they brought the lens in, and the hero faded on every walk through a door); in_shoulder_rate: 1/s the root eases in to that clearance (a tenth of a second: a door frame comes into the side cast all at once, and moved there in one frame the lens jumped 0.2 m). feelers: degrees either side of the arm where a sphere is cast (Lyra's predictive avoidance, design/research/pages/camera/lyra-penetration-opentournament.md, which uses 16 and 32 with weights); feel_pitch: the same above and below the arm, so a look up does not thread the lens under the rover nor a look down over a wall's top; feel_thin: the widest feeler that also looks for thin things; feel_slack: m of arm a feeler's hit allows for every degree the feeler inside it is off the arm (the first allows none: what it meets may be anywhere up to the arm), so what they allow is a cone round each obstacle and never changes faster than feel_slack against the view's turn; at 80 degrees it is 4.24 m, the arm at the default pitch (distance 4.2), so an obstacle is felt from the first degree it could matter; feel_rate: m/s the lens moves in toward what the feelers allow, and at most out again (7.5 m/s is 0.125 m a frame, under tests/indoor_test.gd's 0.15 m step with a walk on top; a turn at stick_deg_per_s, 140, times feel_slack is 7.4 m/s, so a key turn is tracked with no lag, and the arm's own cut is left only what changed in the last 3 degrees, 0.12 m of it eased); thin_tail: m before where the lens would stand in which thin things count (layer 3: posts, but also every machine narrower than the hero's 0.95 m): the lens stops before one it would stand in, where it used to pass through and show its inside; nearer the hero they stay ignored and draw in front of it (pulling in for a post shoves the lens into the hero's back, rule 4). All art direction but the half-diagonal
camera.note_in: third person inside a room (data/world.json rooms; follow_cam.gd; design/research/interior-camera.md). We found no shipped third-person game that forces first person indoors; engines and guides keep the follow camera and tighten it (a camera volume's profile, 'a more claustrophobic camera mode' for a narrow corridor; a shorter arm and a shoulder offset on one blend value, the UE spring arm guide; 'set a max distance that fit your levels', GameDev Pensieve). Playtest 14 Nov: first person indoors dropped for third person. in_ease_s: s the blend may take from 0 to 1 at most (it follows the hero's distance to the door, so a walk sets the pace; a teleport is capped by this); in_approach: m from the door at which the profile starts to blend in, so the arm is short before it meets the door frame; in_distance: the arm at the default pitch indoors, sized to HAB 1's plan (radius 2.4 m: the lens stays in the room behind a hero at its middle); a room whose plan is shallower takes that depth instead (the storm shelter's 1.75 m half-depth, follow_cam.gd _fit()); in_shoulder: m the arm's root sits right of the hero (an over-the-shoulder Socket Offset; the UE spring arm guide shows 0.55 m for a full shoulder view, design/research/pages/camera/ue-springarm-uhiyama.md; 0.35 m here is art direction for a 4.8 m room); in_pivot_height: m over the floor, a little lower than outside so the lens stays under a 2.3 m ceiling at the default pitch; in_pitch_min and in_pitch_max: degrees, narrower than outside so a look down does not press the lens into the ceiling; in_keep: m the arm's root must be past the plan's edge before the plan holds the lens fully (it blends in from the edge), so walking in the lens comes through the door with the hero, about a body's width (reality.json hero.width 0.95) and never so close that the hero fades; the feelers that pull the lens in before the arm meets a wall or a door frame work indoors and out (note_clear). All else art direction
camera.note_frame: frame_low: share of the frame height the pivot sits below centre when looking level (1/6 is the lower-third line), easing to centred at pitch_min; slope_ahead: m ahead along the view where a ray reads the ground; slope_share: share of that slope the view pitches by; slope_max_deg: the most it pitches. follow_rate and lead_rate also set the lead that cancels the spring's lag in a steady walk (2 v / follow_rate, built at lead_rate)

interact.note_wiper: wiper_s: real seconds a solar row's wiper takes from one end of the row to the other (a use row's `wiper`, data/world.json uses). Art direction (no source): the rows' electric wipers are this game's own device
interact.note_curtain: curtain_gather: an open curtain's width as a share of its closed width, gathered at its jamb (HAB 1's toilet). Art direction
interact.note_reach: reach: m from the body's axis to the nearest point of the thing's collision box (either side of a door), height counted only past the feet or the head; cone_deg: in third person the thing's shape must lie inside this cone (both sides) round the heading. stick_deg: the current target counts this much nearer the aim, at the cone's edge and against a rival, so the prompt does not flicker (skills/character-body, Using things). All three art direction

hop.note: xfade: s of blend between clips; anticipation: s of crouch before take-off, the last part of hop_start plays in it (all 0.34 s of it would delay every press); xfade_hop: s of blend into and out of the hop clips, short so the arc keeps its timing
hop.note_fall: fall_after: s off the floor before the model leaves its walk for the fall clip (hero_model.gd). A one-frame drop over a bevel (HAB 1's hatch sill, 1.5 cm down to the deck) played hop_air and restarted the walk cycle: the legs reset on the threshold (14 Nov playtest). The same 0.1 s as input.coyote, the grace in which the ground still counts for a jump

hero.note: gait_hysteresis: Froude the hurry-to-walk change sits below hero.froude.walk_run. The boots' sink is reality.json hero.sink; smooth_deg: at load the hero's normals are averaged across edges flatter than this angle, so the suit's folds shade smooth and the pack's box corners (90 deg) stay sharp; the limbs are about eight-sided, 45 deg a face, which 40 left faceted (the file's normals were split face by face)
hero.note_hurry: hurry_still_s: s with no move input after which the hurry lock (player.gd hurrying: a press locks it, the next press lets go) lets go by itself, so a kid who stops and walks on later is not surprised by a run. Art direction, never shown to players
hero.note_step: step_catch_s: s the drawn body takes to catch up a whole step (reality.json hero.step) after the body steps up or down at once: it follows at hero.step / step_catch_s m/s and is never more than a step behind. Source's SmoothViewOnStairs does this to the view (150 units/s, an 18-unit step, 18 / 150 = 0.12 s; design/research/pages/camera/source-sdk-2013-smooth-stairs.md); here the whole drawn body, so the feet do not pop up a sill (the greenhouse's 0.18 m threshold rose in one frame)

coat.note: Where the suit gathers the design's dust coat (DESIGN.md weathering: its colour, its amount by sky state, each role's share; the visor's share is 0), by analogy with Apollo: dust 'quickly and effectively coated' boots, gloves and suits, and wore through 'above boot' (Gaier 2005); no Mars EVA has happened. legs_top: m above the soles where the kicked-up dust has faded out (the knee is about 0.5 m up); knees: the front of the thighs, knees and shins (kneeling, falls); hands, forearms: gloves and forearms (tools and samples); torso: helmet shell, chest and back, light; pack_top: the top of the backpack, by how level it is; patch: m across a patch of thicker or thinner dust; max: the most of the coat any part shows; chroma: the share of the dust's hue the suit takes (the rest is its brightness, a grey-brown stain): with the dust's full hue the storm turned the suit orange, and an orange astronaut vanishes against Mars (project rule). Both keep the hero a dusty white with readable teal bands. All art direction, judged in day and storm captures.

audio.note: The mix (audio/audio.gd). dB on top of the files, which are normalised (loops -20 LUFS, one-shots -3 dBFS peak). range: m, a 3D sound's cut-off, Mars sound 'falters at just 26 feet (8 meters)' (NASA/JPL 2022); unit_size: m where a 3D sound starts to fall away. fade_s: s of the inside/outside crossfade. breath: rest in breaths a minute, a resting adult takes 12 to 18 (MedlinePlus, Vital signs); hard (at the sheet's hurry speed), rise_s and fall_s (time constants: up fast, settling back slowly) and inhale_share (where in a breath the exhale starts) are art direction, never shown to players. wind: ref_speed m/s that plays at wind.db (sky states blow 4 to 6, world.json weather); gust: the swell's share; gust_hz: its slow noise frequency. habitat and machines: world.json item ids. pitch: random spread on one-shots. music: db of a cue (files at about -16 LUFS), fade_s its fade in, gap_s the least silence between two cues (rare by design: skills/living-atmosphere), art direction, never shown to players

rover.note: audio/audio.gd, art direction: the motor loop plays from pitch_min at a stand to pitch_max at the rover's top speed (an electric drive whines higher as it spins faster), at motor_idle of its full loudness standing; the wheels' crunch is silent standing, loudest at top speed and pitched over wheels_pitch

audio.note_bed: art direction, audio/audio.gd. sounds: dB per file on top of its -3 dBFS peak. breath.exert_db: the respirator loop under the breaths at the sheet's hurry speed, silent at rest. bed: one phrase of a calm piece (files at about -16 LUFS) at db, duck_db lower while a cue plays, fade_s to let a phrase go when the hero goes in or out, then a rest of rest_s (random in the range) after a phrase ends; none in the first first_s of a session nor within after_cue_s of a cue's end (Breath of the Wild's field-music habit, design/plans/next-lanes.md 4.2). duck_db: the suit, outside and inside sound under a cutscene that calls audio.duck(true)
audio.note_radio: art direction, audio/audio.gd. radio: the suit radio (Suit bus, clear: a radio is not heard through the air or the helmet), wordless so nothing tells a story before 14 Nov. db on top of the -3 dBFS files; gap_s the least time between two radio sounds ("every minute or two", design/research/alive.md touch-up 12; Mission Control talks "fairly regularly", Reisman); base_s: the base calls at a random time in this range; wait_s: a radio sound waits this long for quiet (no music cue, no event sound), then is dropped. motif: the rare quiet-moment cue (audio/music/<name>.ogg, made by assets-cache/music/ours/make_motifs.py), at most once in gap_s, after the hero stands below still_speed m/s outside for still_s, or the first time the dust devil is within devil_centre of the middle of the view (share of the width); never in the first after_s of a session, when the bed is still settling

rover.note: sandbox/rover.gd, art direction (the physical rows are reality.json rover.*). travel: m each wheel's suspension takes up either way before the body tilts; wheel_shade and body_shade: [radius m, strength 0 to 1] of the moving contact shadow under each wheel pair and under the body's two halves (world.touch(), shaded like data/world.json grounding)
rover.note_speed: speed you can feel (13 Nov playtest: "I felt the rover is slow"), art direction: the wheels' dust stream's strength is (speed / top) ^ dust_power, so a crawl throws a wisp and full speed a full stream (the grains already leave at the tread's speed, world/dust.gd); track_depth: a wheel print's depth at a crawl and at top speed (terrain.mark strength), so a fast run leaves a darker track
rover.note_spring: the drawn body on its springs over the wheels (sandbox/rover.gd _spring), held inside `travel`. hz: its bounce; passenger cars ride at 0.5 to 1.5 Hz (OptimumG Springs & Dampers tech tip 1), and a spring sized for the same sag under Mars weight bounces sqrt(3.71 / 9.81) = 0.61 times as fast, 0.31 to 0.92 Hz (our derivation). damping: share of critical, a little under it (art direction: one small overshoot at a stop, then still; passenger cars sit near 0.15 to 0.45, Milliken via forum citations). roll_deg_g: degrees of lean out of a turn per g of sideways acceleration in the planet's own g; sedans 1.0 to 1.8 (Milliken via OptimumG tech tip 2), no rover or truck number found, so a tall cab on long travel leans more by art direction: a full-speed turn (2.8 m/s at 20 deg/s, 0.26 Mars g) leans about 1.6 deg. pitch_deg_g: nose up setting off, down braking, per g of the speed change (less than roll: art direction). Excerpts: design/research/pages/alive/rover-spring-and-radio.md

life.note: The hero's layers on top of its clips (player/hero_life.gd), art direction judged on film; the limits that are physical come from the sheet (hero.lean.max). lean_share: share of the free-body angle atan(a / g) the upper body leans into a push; lean_hz and lean_damping: its spring (under 1 swings a little past upright at a stop); carry_lean_deg: extra forward lean over a carried bag; breath_chest_deg and breath_shoulder_deg: how far the chest tips back and the shoulders rise at a full breath (the clock and rate are audio.breath's); look_waist_deg, look_head_deg, look_pitch_deg: each side, the waist takes most of a turn because a helmet turns with the torso (no sheet row: suited neck and waist ranges were not found); look_rate: 1/s the gaze's angles ease toward a new aim (angles, not the point: a point eased across the body flips the turn); look_far: m ahead along the camera's view the gaze rests when nothing is near; the waist's share fades out with the pace (a walker looks with the head). carry_swing_deg: each arm swings out about the vertical at the shoulder while a bag is held, so the gloves and forearms meet its sides instead of going into it; carry_out: m the bag rides ahead of the clip's hold point, so the chest does not go into its back (the clip was posed for a thinner bag); both found with tests/player_test.gd carry_hands (the drawn hero at most 1 cm inside the cargo bag over a walk cycle); at 10 deg one glove grazed the bag's side by 1.0 cm at one phase of the walk clip, so the real-time test passed or failed by which frames it sampled; 12 leaves no vertex inside; carry_swing_s: s to swing in or out, the clip's crossfade

lamps._note: the helmet lights (player/suit_lamps.gd). Real: 'EMU lights are found on either side of the astronaut's helmet and are used to illuminate objects in space; the lights have their own battery system' (NASA, spaceflight.nasa.gov/station/eva/spacesuit.html, archived at webarchive.library.unt.edu/eot2008). Two lamp faces, one unshadowed spot between them (one light pass, not two). on_deg, off_deg: sun elevation they switch on below and off above outside, the base lamps' own 2 and 6 degrees (sky.lamps_on_deg) so suit and base agree. side_m, up_m, ahead_m: each face from the visor's middle (hero_model eye), in the head's frame; tilt_deg: the beam pitched down to light the ground ahead. energy, range_m, angle_deg, fade_s: art direction (14 Nov), judged in a night capture
lamps._look: how the lit lamps read (player/lamp_glow.gdshader), all art direction (15 Nov playtest: 'the light beam is not visible coming through it', 'just 2 white dots'), judged in night captures from behind, the side and the front. bulb_glow: a lamp face's emission energy in the lamp's colour (DESIGN.night.md lighting.lamp.color), high enough to bloom where the preset has glow; beam_m, beam_deg: the length and half angle of the cone of light in the air ahead of each lamp, short of the ground so it never draws a line on it; beam_glow: how much light the cone adds beside the lamp seen from the side (up to five times that seen along it, from behind the hero: the shader's sight term), fading to none at its far end and its outline; halo_m, halo_glow: the radius and strength of the glare round a lamp seen from in front, for presets with no glow

sky._note: the world's own clock (world/sky_clock.gd, design/research/day-cycle.md section 5, skills/day-cycle). It drives the look only: no sol counter, nothing scored (hard rule 1 until 14 Nov). day_minutes: real minutes a whole sol takes (12 to 24; Minecraft 20, Breath of the Wild 24, Subnautica about 20), with the night night_speed times faster than the day (Subnautica's split: 4 min 30 s of night in 20), so about 16.7 minutes of light, the long dusk at full speed, and 3.3 of night; the night is where the sun is below the night key's elevation (DESIGN.night.md celestial.hour), ramping in over night_ramp_deg above it. start_hour: local solar time the session starts, 06:30, just after sunrise (the first sunset about 12 minutes in). sol_s: a mean sol in seconds (Mars24, NASA GISS: 24 h 39 min 35.244 s), how the stars and moons keep pace with the sun
sky._look: look_hz: how often a second the sky, ambient, fog, lamps, coat and wind take the clock's blend (a step of a tenth of a second moves a 75 s dusk by 0.13%, unseen); sun_step_deg: 0 turns the light with the sun every frame, as smoothly as its disc (13 Nov playtest: 1 degree steps eased over burst_s read as shadows that 'wait, then teleport fast-forward'); above 0 the light follows in burst_s eased bursts each time the sun has moved that far, sun_step_low_deg below low_deg of sun. Measured at 16:30 with a still camera, 4 s: flickering pixels 2.96% continuous against 3.52% in 1 degree steps (Gaming), 2.17% against 1.69% (Phone; 1.64% with the clock stopped, PIP and the dust); light_swap_deg: the sun elevation at which the one light changes from the sun to the night design's fill, both dark there, each fading over light_band_deg down to light_floor (energy, the sun's and an off lamp's) and the fog's sun scatter to scatter_floor: the renderer specialises every material on a light reaching it and on scatter over 0.001, so crossing either compiled them all again at the first dusk (rasterizer_scene_gles3.cpp 4.7.2, measured); probe_step: how far the four keys' shares must move (summed) before the outdoor reflection probes are redrawn, about 8 times a sol. All art direction
sky._lamps: the base's lamps switch on below lamps_on_deg of sun and off above lamps_off_deg (hysteresis, the research's 2 and 6 degrees), each lamp up to lamps_stagger_deg apart so the base does not flip like a switchboard, fading over lamps_fade_s. Art direction
sky._debug: skip_s: real seconds of time-lapse the debug sky key takes to the next phase (dawn, noon, dusk, night, then a storm at noon); storm_build_h: game hours a storm takes to blow in or clear on the key (a real global storm builds over days and its haze e-folds in 43 sols, Guzewich 2019: too slow to see in a sandbox). Art direction
sky._dust: dust that settles and stays (design/research/day-cycle.md rows 22 to 27): the weathering coat climbs from DESIGN.md's amount to DESIGN.storm.md's over coat_rise_h game hours of storm and stays after it, clearing back with an e-fold of coat_clear_sols sols (panels on Mars lose about 0.2% a sol to dust and get it back only in rare wind cleaning events, Lorenz 2021; art direction, so a session sees it go); every panel takes the storm's coat, and wears the rules' dust (sim.json panel_dust: the night gust, 0.2% a sol) as the whole coat once it reaches panel_full (the gust's 0.33, so the morning after shows it plainly; art direction); a row's wiper clears its own, the dust gone behind the bar as it passes (sandbox/interactions.gd: the wipers are this game's own device, not presented as a NASA plan). Wind: night_wind times the night row's speed after dark (Gale's downslope winds peak at night, about 21 m/s against 14 by day: Martinez 2017, Ullan 2017); the far whirlwind only between devil_hours (Gale's vortices peak 11:00 to 13:00 LTST, about one a sol, Newman 2019; it shows into the early afternoon)
